subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated identical exec commands with the same nonzero structured outcome count as no progress even when their output changes meaningfully?
rationale: Source and live proof establish that output-sensitive hashing permits runaway loops, but dropping all nonzero output from identity can deliberately block legitimate retry workflows; repository history treats that false-positive budget as an owner-level availability policy.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprint
options.body: Approve the safety tradeoff, refresh the branch against current main, and merge with the existing structured identity and regression coverage.

options.title: Require a narrower progress signal
options.body: Keep nonzero output partly progress-sensitive and define an owner-approved normalization or command-class policy before merging.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Leave the linked bug open if maintainers prefer missed loop detection over the potential false-positive blocking surface.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprint
recommendation.body: Approve the safety tradeoff, refresh the branch against current main, and merge with the existing structured identity and regression coverage.
